title: Musical family: parents, circus-clarinet uncle, organ and Scott Joplin
summary: Both parents were vocal teachers, an uncle played circus clarinet and another uncle played ragtime on the family organ; his younger sister was not musical.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Garvin, can I back up a little bit and ask you a couple of questions? For example, are you from a

Yes, yes, yes. I guess it was passed on. My mother was a vocal teacher and a fine singer, and my father was also a vocal teacher. And I had an uncle who played clarinet in the circus and, as I say, my family -- we didn't get a piano until about 1909, but before --

Yes, when I came on the scene we had an organ, one of those pedal things that you pedal, you know? And I had also an uncle who played piano and he would come over and play Scott Joplin on the organ, you know, -- or ragtime, it wasn't necessarily Scott Joplin, but in later years, say, in 1911 or 12, he was playing Maple Leaf Rag, I remember distinctly. Scott Joplin.
Let me ask you another question. Are there sisters and brothers that you have in your family?
I have a sister, but she never was interested in music. She lives in Denver now -- in the mid-west in Denver, Colorado.
